title: Enable rootless BuildKit runners, incremental linter cache, and adaptive cache priming
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: Replace privileged Docker-in-Docker build jobs with rootless BuildKit runners across our primary CI pools; introduce an incremental linter cache (ESLint/ruff/tsc) keyed by source + tool version; implement an adaptive cache priming daemon that pre-warms remote cache shards based on recent commit patterns and graph heuristics.

Why: Current CI jobs require privileged containers for some build stages (image build/privileged mounts) which increases risk and complicates running CI on shared runners and remote providers. Cold-build latency and repeated lint passes are a major contributor to developer iteration time. Adaptive priming will reduce tokenized cache-miss bursts during rollout windows.

Non-goals: This ticket does not onboard private on-prem runners nor change production image signing policies (that will be follow-ups). We will not change upstream toolchain versions here except where required to enable rootless operation.

Design highlights and trade-offs: 
- Rootless BuildKit: runs daemonless user-mode buildkitd (moby/buildkit rootless mode or nerdctl+rootlesscontainers). Pros: removes CAP_SYS_ADMIN requirement, safer for shared pools. Cons: requires userns/kernel support on runners and careful UID/GID mapping for cache owner paths.
- Incremental linter cache: store tool caches in remote object store (s3-like) with keys = sha256(source_files_glob + tool_version + relevant config). Pros: large speedups on repeated lint runs; Cons: additional IO and potential cache TTL management complexity.
- Adaptive priming daemon: lightweight service that looks at commit diffs, dependency graph churn, and recent cache hit rates to decide which cache artifacts to prefetch into regional cache shards during low load windows. Trade-off: more operational surface area vs. reduced first-hour CI backpressure.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) All existing CI image build jobs in the linux shared pool have a non-privileged rootless path that reduces required capabilities to none or minimal.
2) Typical cold build time for frontend/service images reduced by >= 20% at the median in the CI shared pool after priming enabled.
3) ESLint/ruff median run time on incremental runs reduced by >= 35% for changed-file-only pushes.
4) No increase in CI flakiness (jobs marked flaky >2% remain unchanged) and no elevated security alerts from infra team during rollout.
5) Documentation for operators (runbook) and developers updated (confluence + README).

Rollout plan: feature-flag the new BuildKit runner per pool, start with the linux-ephemeral pool (canary), monitor build latency and failure modes for 72hrs, then expand to linux-shared. Enable incremental linter cache as an opt-in env var for repos then flip default after 2 weeks of canary telemetry. Start adaptive priming in passive mode (estimate-only) for one week before enabling active prefetch.

Metrics to track: build wall time distribution, cache hit rate, cache miss cost (tokens), lint job duration, CI failure rate, runner kernel userns availability telemetry, and number of jobs falling back to privileged path.
